nodes.name: Co Single Atom Anchoring on MoS2
nodes.procedure: Before being loaded into the vacuum chamber, the monolayer MoS2 was transferred to glassy carbon by a PMMA-assisted wet transfer process. Under the guidance of theoretical calculation, the simple and effective LMBE method was employed to directly anchor Co SAs on the monolayer MoS2 (more details can be seen in Experimental Methods in the Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image of monolayer MoS2 shows no visible impurities, grain boundaries, or defects with interplanar spacing of 0.27 nm consistent with (100) crystal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure and crystalline quality of monolayer MoS2 were studied by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM). There are no visible impurities, grain boundaries, and defects in Figure 1a, indicating that the monolayer MoS2 is a planar structure with good crystallinity and uniformity. The interplanar spacing is 0.27 nm, which is consistent with the (100) crystal plane of MoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS shows clear Co L3 and Co L2 edges, confirming the presence of Co single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Figure 1d, EELS extracted from the red rectangle of the STEM image in Figure 1c shows clearly the CoL3 and CoL2 edges, demonstrating that the brighter spot in the area represents a Co single atom.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES verifies Co content of 1.07 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES), it is verified that the content of Co is 1.07 wt% (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test HAADF-STEM shows no noticeable cluster formation, confirming good morphology and crystalline structure stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Obviously, HAADF-STEM after the long-term stability test in Figure 5b presents no noticeable cluster, and the SA loading change proves a good morphology and crystalline structure stability in Co@MoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: S 2p and Mo 3d XPS spectra show identical chemical valence states before and after stability test with no binding energy shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5c,d displays the XPS characterizations of Co@MoS2 before and after the AMF-assisted amperometric j-t test, which exhibits the identical chemical valence states without a binding energy shift of the S 2p and Mo 3d core levels.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Co@MoS2 is 19.23 mF cm^-2 and MoS2 is 5.13 mF cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S8, the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) value of Co@MoS2 is 19.23 mF cm^-2, which is larger than that of MoS2 (5.13 mF cm^-2), proving that Co SA anchoring can bring more active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra confirm monolayer thickness of MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra and atomic force microscopy (AFM) were employed to determine the thickness of MoS2, showing that the fabricated film is a monolayer (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: VSM shows in-plane magnetic hysteresis loop at 300 K for Co@MoS2, confirming room-temperature ferromagnetism, while MoS2 is nonmagnetic.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Experimentally, magnetic measurements using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) indeed verified the magnetic behavior of MoS2 and Co@MoS2. The magnetization versus magnetic field (M-H) curves in Figure 2e and Figure S6 show that the Co@MoS2 exhibiting an evident in-plane magnetic hysteresis loop at the temperatures of 5 and 300 K displays in-plane room-temperature ferromagnetism.
